The vector equation has no solutions, so {{v}} is not a linear combination.

content.p: If possible demonstrate how to construct a specific linear combination of {{veclist}} that equals {{v}}.

intro.p: Let \mathbf{v_1} and \mathbf{v_2} and \mathbf{b} be given by the figure below. Is \mathbf{b} a linear compbintation of \mathbf{v_1} and \mathbf{v_2}? Explain why or why not, and find a set of weights, if one exists. ( Note: there is no scale on the axes, so you can't determine coordinates for the various vectors; just use the grid and figure appropriately. )
